Site handover24-Nov-2025

Scope: roads, storm water piping with catch basins, manholes, box culvert and channels, sewerage network with a sewage lift station, potable water and TSE networks with fire hydrants, 36 kV medium-voltage cables with ring main units, and street lighting. Contract duration 18 months.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At 96.5% against 77.8% planned under the revised plan, the project is 18.7% ahead. This week it gained only 0.36% against 1.35% planned, and the earthworks-for-plots and road-works milestones, both forecast for 13-Oct-2026, are still open.

Well ahead overall, but this week fell short of plan and two milestones are past their forecast. The weekly report forecast both the earthworks for plots and the road works to finish on 13-Oct-2026. The P6 update (data date 20-Oct-2026) still shows both as not started, scheduled for the data date, and lists them as failed starts. Project completion is forecast for 19-Jan-2027 in the weekly report and 14-Jan-2027 in P6, both well before the contract date of 23-May-2027.

Data notes

  • The weekly report's headline, the Tracking Sheet and the summary sheets label a cost-based progress figure as "actual". This report uses physical % complete (man-hours) only: 96.5% against 77.75% planned. The Look Ahead file also gives a progress figure for the end of Q3 2026 without stating its basis, so it is not used.
  • The report states its own week number (Report No. 48, Week-48), which is used here. Counting whole weeks from site handover (24-Nov-2025 to 20-Oct-2026, 330 days) gives week 47.
  • This-week values: the latest report gives only this week's and last week's cumulative man-hours, so the S-curve table has two rows, and it gives no previous-week quantities, so "This week" in the scope table is blank.
  • Earned man-hours exceed the budget in seven phases (up to 128% for the open drain channel), and planned man-hours also exceed the budget in three of them. The baseline and revised plans use different totals (406,229 and 406,774 man-hours). The forecast column of the Physical-Chart Data sheet shows 93.7% for October, below the 96.5% actual.
  • The milestone "Complete delivery of all equipment and materials" is marked achieved on 06-Oct-2026, but the procurement log has 9 items "under manufacturing" and one at 4 of 7, and the Procurement Summary has 27 of 34 materials on site. The log lists 36 items, the summary 34.
  • Completion dates differ between files: 19-Jan-2027 (weekly report forecast), 14-Jan-2027 (P6), 23-Nov-2026 (Tracking Sheet target and Look Ahead), and 23-May-2026 as the contract end in the "work done this week" file (the contract end is 23-May-2027).
  • Milestone baselines differ between the Milestones sheet and P6: electrical networks 06-May-2027 vs 04-Jan-2027, project completion 23-May-2027 vs 14-Jun-2027.
  • Scope quantities disagree between sheets: storm water 3,791 m (Progress Summary) vs 3,971 m of GRP pipe (Major Quantities); MV network 13,171 m vs 5,632 of 15 kV cable. The Major Quantities sheet gives curbs in m³ and MV cable in m². Telecom supply shows 6,395 m delivered against 11,025 m installed.
  • Shop drawing totals differ: 394 (dashboard), 703 (Quality-Stat sheet) and 621 (Tracking Sheet).
  • Manpower for October: the dashboard shows 61 planned and 181 actual manual workers (by trade), the Manpower sheet 136 and 156.
  • Other files name the consultant EGIS as contractor (Look Ahead), give the PM as Abdullah Alshunaifi, and place the project in the central sector instead of the western sector. The invoice summary counts 3 paid invoices, but the paid amount equals invoices 1 to 6. Several cells show #REF! (issue owners, EAC). The FIR summary has dates such as 25-Aug-2062.
